# EvTag

> A tag is a small label that marks an item with a keyword, category, or attribute. It can carry a leading icon and an optional close button to remove it.

| ID | `evoq-ui:tag` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |

| Source | `src/atoms/tag/EvTag.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<span class="ev-tag">` |
| Used inside | `evoq-ui:tag-group` (EvTagGroup) |

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Tag**, frame `4105:63441` (Tag). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use to label an item with a keyword, category, status, or attribute.
- Use a removable tag (with close) for user-applied filters or selections.
- Use a leading icon to reinforce the tag's type or meaning.
- Use the outline style for a lighter, lower-emphasis label.

### When not to use

- Don't use to trigger an action  →  use Button (`evoq-ui:button`)
- Don't use for a standalone status  →  use Badge (`evoq-ui:badge`)
- Don't use for navigation between views  →  use Tabs (`evoq-ui:tabs`)
- Don't use long phrases or sentences as a tag.

### Do

- Keep labels short (1–2 words), sentence case
- Show the close icon only when the tag is removable
- Group related tags and let them wrap
- Use a consistent variant within one group

### Don't

- Pack a long sentence into a tag
- Mix removable and static tags without a cue
- Use color alone to convey meaning
- Use tags as primary navigation

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvTag`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<span class="ev-tag">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:tag` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
